notes: PSA 5 ng/mL. PI-RADS 2. PSAD 0.10. Prostate volume 49 mL. csPCa 0.82.

note_sections.t: The patient attends this multidisciplinary consultation to discuss definitive management options following the recent confirmation of prostate adenocarcinoma.

Long-standing referral for biochemical progression of prostate-specific antigen levels culminating in recent tissue diagnosis. The patient is a recently retired logistics manager who continues to maintain an active lifestyle through regular cycling, though he reports mild mechanical joint discomfort managed with as-needed paracetamol. He resides alone but maintains close contact with his spouse, who serves as his primary support during medical appointments. Social history is notable for a past smoking habit of 29 pack-years, discontinued over a decade ago, alongside moderate alcohol consumption of five units weekly. Recent routine health maintenance has included a standard chest radiograph, seasonal influenza immunization, and a scheduled dental examination, all of which were uneventful. He acknowledges significant apprehension regarding invasive procedures and has requested additional time to thoroughly review all available therapeutic pathways.

Per rectum, the prostate gland is palpated as smooth and symmetrical without discrete nodules or asymmetry, correlating with a clinical stage of cT1c. General inspection reveals a well-nourished gentleman with a body mass index of 32.4, and cardiovascular auscultation is unremarkable with a regular pulse of 79 beats per minute. Peripheral joint examination demonstrates mild crepitus in the knees consistent with his known osteoarthritis.

admin: Patient anxious about procedures — allocate extra consult time.
